title: Regional ice date offset had a positive relation to Superior-minus-Erie cover contrast in 1973-2026
abstract: We tested whether the regional ice peak date changes relative to mean lake timing with the Superior-minus-Erie maximum ice cover contrast. We used 54 winters in a fixed NOAA GLERL summary table. After adjustment for mean cover and year, a 10 percentage point increase in the contrast gave a 1.40 day later regional date relative to the four-lake mean. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was 0.20 to 2.28 days. Seven of eight planned checks also had positive intervals. The 2011-2026 check had an interval from -0.83 to 3.16 days. The mean absolute regional offset was 7.57 days. This result shows a composition-related timing association in the full summary record. It does not establish a physical cause, a recent-period effect or forecast skill. Changing chart frequency, unknown peak tie rules, an equal-weight four-lake reference and one source snapshot limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate results, checks, provenance and a figure. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Three groups of 18 winters show the regional peak date offset and cover contrast. Bars show one standard error. The fitted line adjusts for mean cover and year. The right panel shows model slopes with conditional 95% block intervals.

citations.reason: Published four-lake spread test and source checks motivated a separate regional-date offset test. The source snapshot overlaps; this is not independent confirmation.
